title: Field action topos with normalized point and coefficient transport
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Use small sites in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite set $P$ put $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over its finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor].

Let $\operatorname{Cond}$ denote sheaves of sets on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings, and $\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}$ its category of internal $\underline G$-actions. There is an equivalence of topoi $E:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}$ with the following normalization. Its underlying condensed sheaf is $(EF)(P)=F(\bar s[P])$. On the dense free subsite of profinite $G$-sets, every map $G\times T\to G\times P$ is uniquely $(g,t)\mapsto(gb(t),f(t))$ with continuous $f:T\to P$ and $b:T\to G$; its restriction agrees with the action-site convention $(f,b)(h,c)=(fh,c\,h^*b)$ of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. These identifications preserve covering families and are natural in profinite tests.

For $p_s:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Cond}$ defined by the test objects [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and $p_G:\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}\to\operatorname{Cond}$ with trivial-action inverse image [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], $Ep_s^{-1}\cong p_G^{-1}$ as finite-product-preserving inverse images. The conjugate right-adjoint comparison identifies $p_{s*}F(P)=F(s[P])$ with the subobject of $F(\bar s[P])$ fixed after every profinite base change. The inclusion is restriction along $\bar s[P]\to s[P]$; the comparison is the sheaf equalizer for this cover with kernel pair $G\times G\times P$ in the profinite $G$-set presentation. In particular, for every commutative condensed ring $R$, this comparison identifies $E(p_s^{-1}R)$ with $R$ with trivial action as ring objects, including multiplication and unit, naturally in ring morphisms.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-field-profinite-galois-site], the qcqs subsite $\mathcal B_s$ is dense and is equivalent, with its induced topology, to $\mathbf{Prof}_G$. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to $\mathcal B_s\subset s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with values in sets. The functor is fully faithful, the topology is induced and every object is covered by the subsite, exactly as required; the sites are small in the stipulated universes, so the required set-valued limits exist. Thus restriction identifies $\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathbf{Prof}_G)$. Write $H$ for the image of $F$. The cited field-site statement identifies $H(P_{\mathrm{triv}})=F(s[P])$ and $H(G\times P)=F(\bar s[P])$, naturally in $P$, and identifies the test map with projection.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9-4.1.10, pp. 27-28; dense-subsite restriction as in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Sites/DenseSubsite/SheafEquiv.lean, IsDenseSubsite instance

proof.text: Let $\mathcal D\subset\mathbf{Prof}_G$ be the full subcategory on $G\times P$, with left translation on $G$. Every $Q$ is covered by $G\times |Q|\to Q$, $(g,q)\mapsto gq$: this is continuous, equivariant and surjective, since $q$ is the image of $(1,q)$. If $v:G\times T\to G\times P$ is equivariant, write $v(1,t)=(b(t),f(t))$. Then $v(g,t)=(gb(t),f(t))$; $f,b$ are continuous by restriction and projection. Conversely this formula is continuous and equivariant for any such $f,b$, and evaluation at $(1,t)$ proves uniqueness. The composite of $(h,c)$ followed by $(f,b)$ sends $(g,u)$ to $(gc(u)b(h(u)),f(h(u)))$, hence is $(fh,c\,h^*b)$, including for noncommutative $G$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28; agent calculation on the free profinite G-objects

proof.text: A finite family $(f_i,b_i):G\times T_i\to G\times P$ is jointly surjective exactly when the $f_i:T_i\to P$ are: for $f_i(t)=p$ the preimage of $(g,p)$ is $(gb_i(t)^{-1},t)$. These are exactly the action-site covering families. This also verifies the induced topology on $\mathcal D$: any covering sieve on a free object contains a finite jointly surjective family $Q_i\to G\times P$; composing with the free covers $G\times |Q_i|\to Q_i$ of step 2 yields a finite free covering family in that sieve. Conversely every such free covering family is covering in $\mathbf{Prof}_G$. Thus $\mathcal D$ is a full dense subsite with precisely the action-site topology. The formulas commute with pullback of profinite parameters. Empty spaces and empty covers satisfy the same statements.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, covering criterion; agent verification of the induced free-subsite topology

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] again, now to $\mathcal D\subset\mathbf{Prof}_G$, using steps 2-3 and the same small set-valued limits. Put $C=\mathbf{Prof}$ with its finite jointly surjective topology and $K=\underline G$, so $K(T)=C(T,G)$. The base site has finite limits. Step 2 identifies $\mathcal D$ with $C_K$, and step 3 identifies their topologies. Now [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] gives $\operatorname{Sh}(C_K)\simeq\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}$. Composing gives $E$. Its underlying sheaf is $M(P)=H(G\times P)=F(\bar s[P])$. For $b:T\to G$ its action is restriction by $(1_T,b)$, so the restriction along $(f,b)$ is $b\cdot f^*$. This proves the asserted sign and order convention and naturality, including on morphisms of sheaves. As an equivalence of topos categories, $E$ and its inverse preserve finite limits.

source.place: Paragraph (3), separable-closure descent infrastructure; agent free-subsite construction using the existing internal-action equivalence

proof.text: The cover $q:G\times P\to P_{\mathrm{triv}}$ has kernel pair $G\times G\times P$ with diagonal left action. Identify it with the free object $G\times(G\times P)$ by $(g,h,p)\mapsto(g,gh,p)$, with inverse $(g_1,g_2,p)\mapsto(g_1,g_1^{-1}g_2,p)$. Its projections are $(g,h,p)\mapsto(g,p)$ and $(g,h,p)\mapsto(gh,p)$. The sheaf equalizer of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] therefore identifies $H(P_{\mathrm{triv}})$, by restriction along $q$, with those $x\in M(P)$ satisfying $\operatorname{pr}_P^*x=h\cdot\operatorname{pr}_P^*x$ in $M(G\times P)$, where $h$ is the first coordinate. Pulling back along $(b,t):T\to G\times P$ says $b\cdot t^*x=t^*x$ for every profinite $T$, $t:T\to P$, $b:T\to G$. Conversely that condition with $T=G\times P$, $b=h$, $t=\operatorname{pr}_P$ gives the equalizer equation. These identifications commute with profinite restriction and with maps of $F$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28; sheaf equalizer (Stacks sites.tex, Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets); explicit free coordinates on the kernel pair

proof.text: Denote the subobject of $M$ in step 5 by $\operatorname{Inv}(M)$. It is a sheaf: local fixed sections glue uniquely in $M$, and their fixedness after each base change is checked on the pulled-back cover by uniqueness. For any condensed sheaf $A$, a sheaf map $A\to\operatorname{Inv}(M)$ is exactly an equivariant map from $A$ with trivial action to $M$: equivariance is precisely that every image section and all its restrictions satisfy the equations of step 5. These inverse factorizations are natural in $A,M$. Since $p_G^{-1}$ is trivial action by [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], this describes its right adjoint $p_{G*}$. Step 5 consequently gives a natural isomorphism $p_{s*}F\simeq p_{G*}EF$, with the required restriction inclusion and universal fixedness, not merely invariance under the abstract elements of $G$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent normalization of the arithmetic/geometric descent adjunction by the sheaf equalizer

proof.text: The point inverse image in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] is a geometric inverse image on sets; its abelian version and right adjoint are the ones specified in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Thus $p_{s*}F(P)=F(s[P])$ is the right adjoint used in step 6. Conjugating $p_s^{-1}\dashv p_{s*}$ by $E$ gives a left adjoint $Ep_s^{-1}$ to $p_{s*}E^{-1}$. Step 6 identifies this right adjoint with $p_{G*}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to obtain the unique natural isomorphism $\alpha:Ep_s^{-1}\simeq p_G^{-1}$ whose mate is exactly the comparison of step 6 (use its inverse for the orientation $R_2\to R_1$ in that lemma). Both functors preserve finite products: $p_s^{-1}$ and $p_G^{-1}$ are geometric inverse images and $E$ is an equivalence. Naturality of $\alpha$ at the two product projections makes its product comparison $\alpha_A\times\alpha_B$, and the terminal comparison is unique.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; agent application to the normalized point right adjoints

proof.text: Apply $\alpha$ to the underlying sheaf of a commutative condensed ring $R$. For every operation $o:R^n\to R$, naturality and the product compatibility of step 7 give $\alpha_R\circ Ep_s^{-1}(o)=p_G^{-1}(o)\circ\alpha_R^n$, using the canonical product comparisons. For $n=0$ this includes the unit and zero; $n=1$ includes negation; $n=2$ includes multiplication and addition. Hence $\alpha_R$ is an isomorphism of ring objects to $R$ with trivial action. Naturality at any ring morphism $R\to R'$ gives the claimed ring-morphism square. For $G=1$ the equalizer has identical arrows and $\alpha$ has the expected trivial-action normalization; for $P=\varnothing$ the sheaf values are terminal. No algebraic closedness, finite Galois group, discreteness of coefficients, or invariant-section exactness was used.
